name: Malediction's damage-taken debuff lasts exactly five direct damage spells (#3921)
contract: Malediction 800776 is a single 64 SPELL_EFFECT_TRIGGER_SPELL on 704120, which carries the whole tooltip: 'increasing the damage they take from your next 5 direct damage spells by $704120s1%'. 704120 effect 0 is aura 271 SPELL_AURA_MOD_DAMAGE_FROM_CASTER, BasePoints 19 -> +20%, with EffectSpellClassMask (262144, 2826240, 0); effect 1 is aura 3 SPELL_AURA_PERIODIC_DAMAGE over DurationIndex 29 = 12000 ms. Spell.dbc gives 704120 ProcCharges 0 and StackAmount 0 and no spell_proc row existed, so Aura::CalcMaxCharges returned 0, Aura::IsUsingCharges was false and the +20% applied to every matching spell for the full twelve seconds instead of the first five. The fix gives 704120 a spell_proc row with Charges 5 and a SpellFamilyMask copied from effect 0's own class mask, so a charge is spent by exactly the spells the bonus applies to. Valanar's Vengeance is inside that mask: every rank 560315/561027-561029/572793-572795 carries SpellFamilyFlags (262144, 0, 0), read directly from Spell.dbc, and a level-80 character owns only 572795. It is DmgClass 1 (MAGIC) and School 32 (Shadow), so its hit raises PROC_FLAG_TAKEN_SPELL_MAGIC_DMG_CLASS_NEG on the victim, which is the row's ProcFlags. Its six-second cast fits inside the twelve-second window, and the final assertion checks the debuff is still present when the charge count is read, so a charge reading of four cannot be an expiry artefact. Malediction's own DoT ticks are periodic and PROC_FLAG_TAKEN_PERIODIC is deliberately absent from the row, so they must not move the count. Known consequence of the shipped record fusing both halves into 704120: once the fifth charge is spent, Aura::ConsumeProcCharges removes the aura and the remaining DoT ticks go with it; only one charge is spent here, so the aura is still present at the last assertion. NOT covered: the tooltip's SP coefficient $sps*0.193333 on the DoT (no spell_bonus_data row, a separate coefficient question), and the 'only from your own Malediction' restriction that the companion CheckProc script enforces - that needs a second Bloodmage attacking the same victim, and the harness has no way to put two casters' damage on one target under two separate Maledictions; a Ghost e2e test would have to put two class-20 characters on one victim, have only the second one cast direct damage spells, and check that the first one's aura_charges on 704120 stay at five.

steps.label: Let spawn AI and level scaling settle
Malediction's debuff lands on the target (native half)
DISCRIMINATING: the debuff carries five charges
Let Malediction's 1500 ms global cooldown (category 133) lapse
DISCRIMINATING: one direct damage spell spends exactly one charge
The debuff is still applied when the charge count is read
